title: Edmonton Oilers change goalies for Game 4, turn to Tristan Jarry
content:
ANAHEIM, Calif. — The Edmonton Oilers, down 2-1 in their first-round playoff series against the Anaheim Ducks and seeking a spark ahead of Sunday’s Game 4, are making a goaltending change.

Tristan Jarry will replace Connor Ingram, Oilers coach Kris Knoblauch told reporters before the game. Ingram, playing behind a brutal Oilers defense, allowed six goals on 38 shots in a 7-4 Game 3 loss. In the first three games combined, Ingram stopped 79 of 93 shots.

“Nothing against Ingram,” Knoblauch said. “I think he’s been solid, but we need our team to play better maybe a few more saves, but hopefully (Jarry) can steal a game and (go on a run). Certainly we feel that we’ve got two good quality goalies.”

It’s the second straight postseason in which the Oilers have made a first-round goaltending change. Calvin Pickard replaced Stuart Skinner last spring against the Los Angeles Kings and helped Edmonton climb out of a 2-0 series hole before Knoblauch switched back to Skinner.

Edmonton acquired Jarry from the Pittsburgh Penguins in Dec. 13 as a theoretical upgrade for Skinner. It didn’t pan out. Jarry put up a .857 save percentage and saved fewer goals than expected in 13 of 19 appearances before losing his job down the stretch to Ingram. Jarry will make his first start since an April 7 overtime loss to Utah.

“He’s been very professional, working on his game and trying to get better,” Knoblauch said. (He’s) not feeling that he was slighted or that this was unfair for him. Very professional, working hard and couldn’t ask anything more of him.”

Game-to-game volatility has been an issue throughout Jarry’s career. He played in two All-Star Games with the Penguins but saw his save percentage steadily decline from .919 in 2021-22 to .893 in 2024-25. Before the trade that sent Skinner to Pittsburgh, Jarry was in a time-share situation with Arturs Silovs. He counts $5.375 million in salary-cap space through 2028 and cost Edmonton three assets to acquire.
